results.title: Numerical simulations of particulate suspensions via a discretized Boltzmann equation. Part 1. Theoretical foundation
results.verification: Cambridge title, author, journal, volume, date, pages, DOI, abstract, and references opened; full article text was not inspected
results.snippet_or_relevance: The paper establishes a discretized Boltzmann framework for fluid-solid suspensions and is part of the early link-wise moving-boundary lineage.
results.allowed_use: Give historical context for representing solid-fluid interaction through population exchange along lattice links.
results.forbidden_use: Do not attribute Ginzburg Eq. (41)-(43), Λ²=1/4, or H_even H_odd=3/16 to this paper.

results.title: Analytic solutions of simple flows and analysis of nonslip boundary conditions for the lattice Boltzmann BGK model
results.verification: DOI metadata and an accessible article copy confirmed title, four authors, Journal of Statistical Physics 87, pages 115-136, and the abstract's slip-velocity analysis
results.snippet_or_relevance: The abstract states that analytic simple-flow solutions are used to analyze nonslip boundary schemes and the slip velocities they generate.
results.allowed_use: Explain that 'bounce-back' is a discrete closure for unknown incoming populations and that its apparent wall location and slip must be analyzed rather than assumed.
results.forbidden_use: Do not transfer its BGK conclusions directly to arbitrary TRT, curved walls, temperature anti-bounce-back, or the Ginzburg forcing gauge.

results.title: Momentum transfer of a Boltzmann-lattice fluid with boundaries
results.verification: AIP DOI, title, authors, Physics of Fluids 13(11), pages 3452-3459, and abstract metadata were cross-checked; publisher full text was not opened
results.snippet_or_relevance: The article studies velocity boundary conditions for curved boundaries and link-wise momentum transfer in the lattice Boltzmann equation.
results.allowed_use: Motivate why a wall cutting a lattice link away from its midpoint needs geometry-aware interpolation or reflection treatment.
results.forbidden_use: Do not use its curved-boundary method as proof that the flat halfway-wall magic condition is universal, and do not apply it to the D2Q5 bulk fourth-order condition.
